# Motor Fuel Prices – October 2025

Tuesday, November 4, 2025

BTS 68-25

Today, the [Bureau of Transportation Statistics (BTS)](https://www.bts.gov/) released [monthly motor fuels prices](https://data.bts.gov/stories/s/Monthly-Motor-Fuel-Prices/gxhw-fwdh/) for October 2025.

In October 2025, the average price for regular motor gasoline was $3.06 per gallon; down 3.3% from September 2025 and down 2.5% from October 2024. 

By region, the average price for regular motor gasoline in October 2025 and year-over-year change was:

* West Coast: $4.18 (up 3.9%)
* Central Atlantic: $3.09 (down 3.1%)
* Rocky Mountain: $3.02 (down 6.7%)
* New England: $2.97 (down 2.2%)
* Midwest: $2.86 (down 5.3%)
* Lower Atlantic: $2.84 (down 3.7%)
* Gulf Coast: $2.62 (down 3.2%)

The average price for diesel no. 2 rose to $3.68 in October 2025, down 1.8% from September 2025, and up 2.6% from October 2024.

Average prices increased by nearly $0.06 during the first two weeks of the month before retreating $0.03 WoW in the third week. ## October 2025 Industry Update: Fuel Prices

Average diesel prices registered little change compared to August.

Monthly Diesel Fuel Rates Line graph

#### Key Points

 The national average price of diesel remained virtually unchanged from August, rising by less than $0.01 from $3.744 to $3.748 in September.
 Compared to September 2024, diesel prices were up 5.4% YoY, or just over $0.19.
 Draws on U.S. Commercial Crude Inventories outpaced builds in September, with inventories falling by -4.2M bbls compared to the consensus of a build of +1.8M bbls for the weeks ending September 5 and September 26.

#### Summary [...] #### Summary

Following the sharp increases observed in June and July, fluctuations in average diesel prices have moderated over the past two months, with combined changes totaling just $0.03 compared to the $0.28 surge recorded earlier in the summer. Despite the relative stability in recent weeks, annual comparisons strengthened notably in September, with average diesel prices rising $0.19 YoY compared to just $0.04 higher YoY in August.

# October 2025 Industry Update: Fuel Prices

[Back to October 2025 Industry Update](https://www.ryantrans.com/news/october-2025-industry-update)

## October 2025 Industry Update: Fuel Prices

Average diesel prices registered little change compared to August.

![Monthly Diesel Fuel Rates Line graph](/sites/default/files/inline-images/P11_28.png)

#### Key Points

* The national average price of diesel remained virtually unchanged from August, rising by less than $0.01 from $3.744 to $3.748 in September.
* Compared to September 2024, diesel prices were up 5.4% YoY, or just over $0.19.
* Draws on U.S. Commercial Crude Inventories outpaced builds in September, with inventories falling by -4.2M bbls compared to the consensus of a build of +1.8M bbls for the weeks ending September 5 and September 26.

#### Summary

Following the sharp increases observed in June and July, fluctuations in average diesel prices have moderated over the past two months, with combined changes totaling just $0.03 compared to the $0.28 surge recorded earlier in the summer. Despite the relative stability in recent weeks, annual comparisons strengthened notably in September, with average diesel prices rising $0.19 YoY compared to just $0.04 higher YoY in August.

On a weekly basis, the [Department of Energy (DOE)/Energy Information Administration (EIA) benchmark diesel price](https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/gasdiesel/) trended mostly upward throughout September. Average prices increased by nearly $0.06 during the first two weeks of the month before retreating $0.03 WoW in the third week. Modest gains resumed in the final two weeks, with a combined increase of approximately $0.02, signaling continued but restrained upward momentum in fuel markets heading into the fourth quarter.

title: EIA Sees Gasoline, Diesel Price Dropping in 2025, 2026 | Rigzone
content:
Another quarterly breakdown included in the EIA’s latest STEO projected that the U.S. on-highway diesel fuel retail price will average $3.69 per gallon in the fourth quarter of 2025, $3.59 per gallon in the first quarter of next year, $3.41 per gallon in the second quarter, $3.47 per gallon in the third quarter, and $3.54 per gallon in the fourth quarter. The U.S. on-highway diesel fuel retail price averaged $3.63 per gallon in the first quarter of 2025, $3.55 per gallon in the second quarter, and $3.76 per gallon in the third quarter, the EIA’s November STEO showed.

“Lower crude oil prices will continue to push down retail gasoline and diesel prices in the United States in 2026,” the EIA said in its latest STEO. [...] The U.S. on-highway diesel fuel retail price is projected to average $3.66 per gallon in 2025 and $3.50 per gallon in 2026 in the EIA’s November STEO. In 2024, the U.S. on-highway diesel fuel retail price averaged $3.76 per gallon, the EIA’s latest STEO highlighted. [...] “We forecast diesel crack spreads to rise from an average of $0.52 per gallon in 2024 to $0.69 per gallon in 2025, reaching $0.84 per gallon in 2026. In the gasoline market, we similarly forecast strong crack spread gains for 2025 and 2026,” the EIA added.

According to the AAA Fuel Prices website, the average price of regular gasoline in the U.S. is $2.998 per gallon, as of December 2. Yesterday’s average was $3.001 per gallon, the week ago average was $3.055 per gallon, the month ago average was $3.036 per gallon, and the year ago average was $3.047 per gallon, the site outlined.

The U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) projected that the U.S. regular gasoline and U.S. on-highway diesel fuel retail price will drop both in 2025 and 2026 in its latest short term energy outlook (STEO).

According to this STEO, which was released on November 12, the EIA sees the U.S. regular gasoline retail price averaging $3.10 per gallon this year and $2.98 per gallon next year. The U.S. regular gasoline retail price averaged $3.31 per gallon in 2024, the EIA’s November STEO showed.

The U.S. on-highway diesel fuel retail price is projected to average $3.66 per gallon in 2025 and $3.50 per gallon in 2026 in the EIA’s November STEO. In 2024, the U.S. on-highway diesel fuel retail price averaged $3.76 per gallon, the EIA’s latest STEO highlighted.

A quarterly breakdown included in the EIA’s latest STEO forecast that the U.S. regular gasoline retail price will come in at $3.02 per gallon in the fourth quarter of 2025, $2.88 per gallon in the first quarter of next year, $3.04 per gallon in the second quarter, $3.09 per gallon in the third quarter, and $2.91 per gallon in the fourth quarter. The U.S. regular gasoline retail price averaged $3.10 per gallon in the first quarter of 2025, $3.16 per gallon in the second quarter, and $3.14 in the third quarter, the EIA’s November STEO showed.
